portrait-of-abraham-de-potter
A man with long dark hair and a rich black coat looks out with a calm, confident face in front of a pale wall. Carel Fabritius painted Abraham de Potter in 1649, and he was a student of Rembrandt.
saint-sebastian-attended-by-saint-irene
A woman holds a torch to look at the wounds of Saint Sebastian, as another woman pulls out an arrow. Georges de La Tour painted this in about 1649, and the torch lights up their serious faces.
the-judgment-of-solomon

King Solomon sits on a throne and points, deciding between two women who both say a baby is theirs, as a soldier holds the child. Nicolas Poussin painted it in 1649, and the true mother's face shows her love for the baby.
american-woman

A woman stands in a tropical landscape of Brazil, with plants and a child at her side. Albert Eckhout, a Dutch painter, made careful pictures of the people, plants and animals of Brazil in the 1640s for the Dutch governor there, and Europeans who had never seen such things were amazed.
christ-in-the-house-of-martha-and-mary

Christ sits at a table with a woman who listens closely, while her sister Martha brings in a basket of bread and looks irritated. Johannes Vermeer painted it in about 1655, and it is the largest painting of his career.
grape-and-melon-eaters

Two ragged boys eat fruit and enjoy it, a boy with a bunch of grapes and another with a slice of melon, while a little dog looks on. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1650, and his street boys are cheerful and warm.
portrait-of-juan-de-pareja

A man with a dark complexion, a wide white collar and a heavy cloak looks out with an intelligent face. Diego Velázquez painted his assistant, Juan de Pareja, in 1650, and Pareja later became a free man and a painter himself.
the-girl-with-the-wine-glass

A young woman in a red dress and a man at a table, with a wine glass, as she looks out at us with a smile. Johannes Vermeer painted it in about 1659, and the light from the stained-glass window is soft.
the-holy-family-with-a-bird
Mary, Joseph and the baby Jesus play with a pet bird and a little dog in a warm, homey scene. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1650, and the family looks like a real Spanish family.
the-jewish-cemetery
Tombstones and ruins of a church stand in a stormy valley, with a waterfall and a rainbow in the sky. Jacob van Ruisdael painted it in about 1655, and the cemetery is a real one in Amsterdam.
the-man-with-the-golden-helmet
A man in a shining helmet looks out of the dark with a shadowed face. The painting was once credited to Rembrandt, but experts now think it was painted by someone in his circle, in about 1650.
the-sciences-and-arts
A grand collection room is filled with globes, instruments, books and paintings, with women who stand for the arts and sciences. Painted by a Flemish artist in about 1650.
the-threatened-swan

A huge white swan hisses, with its wings spread, to protect its nest from a dog, with a farmer in the back. Jan Asselijn painted it in about 1650, and it is said to be a symbol of a Dutch statesman standing up to enemies.
the-young-beggar

A ragged boy sits in a doorway, picking fleas from his shirt, in a patch of sunlight. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1650, and the boy's bare feet and dirty clothes are shown with sympathy.
virgin-and-child-with-a-rosary
Mary and the baby Jesus hold a rosary, and the two look warm and gentle in a quiet picture. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1650.
a-woman-with-a-basket-of-beans-in-a-garden
A woman and a child sit in a sunlit garden, with a basket of beans, near a wall. Pieter de Hooch painted it in 1651, and the quiet, everyday scene is full of light.
a-view-of-delft

A narrow, curved view of a Dutch street in Delft shows a man at a stall selling a viola da gamba, with a statue and a bench. Carel Fabritius painted it in 1652, and the picture is made to look right in a special viewing box.
castle-bentheim
A castle sits high on a hilltop, lit by the sun, with a stormy sky and a path leading up to it. Jacob van Ruisdael painted it in 1653, and the real castle is in Germany.
bathsheba-at-her-bath
Bathsheba sits holding a letter from the king, and looks down thoughtfully while a servant dries her feet. Rembrandt painted it in 1654, and it is a very quiet and sad picture.
samson-and-delilah-guercino
Samson, asleep, lies in the lap of a woman while a man cuts off his hair, and soldiers wait to catch him. Guercino painted it in 1654.
the-gallant-conversation-known-as-paternal-admonition

A man in a dark coat speaks to a young woman in a fine satin dress, who looks down while drinking, as a woman behind them looks at us. Gerard ter Borch painted it in about 1654, and his beautiful silk has been admired for centuries.
the-goldfinch

A little bird sits on a feeder chained to a wall, in a bright light. Carel Fabritius painted it in 1654, a few months before he was killed when the powder magazine in Delft exploded. Donna Tartt's novel The Goldfinch is named for it.
the-sentry
A soldier sits asleep against a wall next to a sleeping dog, with a gun and a little town gate behind him. Carel Fabritius painted it in 1654.
young-man-in-a-fur-cap
A young man in a fur cap and a heavy coat looks out with a calm, direct look in front of a pale wall. This is probably a self-portrait painted by Carel Fabritius in about 1654.
a-mayor-of-delft-and-his-daughter
A man in a hat sits in a chair holding a letter, while a young girl stands beside him and looks at us. Jan Steen painted it in 1655, and the man is Adriaan van der Werff, the mayor of Delft.
boy-with-a-dog
A boy with a dog shows a bright, friendly look as he holds the dog's collar, and the dog jumps up. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1655.
las-hilanderas

Women spin and wind wool in the front of a room, and in the back there is a tapestry with the story of Arachne. Diego Velázquez painted it in about 1655, and the spinning wheel is painted so fast it looks like a blur.
saint-hugh-in-the-carthusian-refectory
A bishop visits a monastery and the monks eat their meal in silence, while a servant brings in food. Francisco de Zurbarán painted it in about 1655, and the white robes of the monks glow.
an-old-woman-dozing
An old woman sits dozing over a Bible with her head on her hand, while a servant peeks in. Nicolaes Maes painted it in about 1656, and he was a student of Rembrandt.
las-meninas

A little princess stands among her ladies-in-waiting, dwarfs and a dog, while the painter, Velázquez, stands at a big canvas, and in a mirror at the back you can see the king and queen. He painted it in 1656, and people still ask who the painting is really about.
the-procuress
A young man puts his arm around a woman while an old woman looks on, and a soldier laughs. Johannes Vermeer painted it in 1656, and he may be the smiling man on the left.
woman-with-a-child-in-a-pantry
A woman holds a child by the hand in a small pantry with a view to a sunlit courtyard. Pieter de Hooch painted it in about 1656, and the paving and the doors make a careful design of squares.
abraham-casting-out-hagar-and-ishmael
Abraham sends his servant Hagar and her young son away into the desert, as a woman looks on from the doorway. Guercino painted it in 1657.
saint-sebastian-preti
Saint Sebastian, with arrows in his body, is tied to a tree, and looks up to heaven in the shadows. Mattia Preti painted it in about 1657.
two-women-at-a-window
A young woman leans out of a window and smiles while an older woman hides behind a shutter, laughing. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1657, and it is a sweet, playful moment.
a-dutch-courtyard

A woman and a girl stand in a quiet brick courtyard behind a house, near a doorway and a wall with a bright blue sky. Pieter de Hooch painted it in 1658, and he loved painting the light in these yards.
allegory-of-fortune

The goddess Fortune sits on a cloud and pours treasure out of a cornucopia onto a crowd of animals, and the animals can't tell the difference between a pearl and a bean. Salvator Rosa painted it in about 1658, and the joke was that rich luck is wasted on fools.
blind-orion-searching-for-the-rising-sun
A blind giant, Orion, with a small guide on his shoulder, walks toward the sunrise to get his sight back, in a misty landscape. Nicolas Poussin painted it in 1658.
cardplayers-in-a-sunlit-room
A group of people sit around a table playing cards in a room with a bright window and a view to a courtyard. Pieter de Hooch painted it in about 1658.
girl-eating-oysters
A girl with a rosy face looks out at you with a sly smile as she is about to swallow an oyster. Jan Steen painted it in about 1658.
girl-reading-a-letter-at-an-open-window

A young woman reads a letter in front of an open window, with her reflection in the glass and a bowl of fruit on the table. Johannes Vermeer painted it in about 1658, and a painted-over Cupid on the wall was found by restorers.
officer-and-laughing-girl

A soldier in a big hat sits with his back to us, talking with a laughing young woman holding a glass, and a map is on the wall behind. Johannes Vermeer painted it in about 1658, and the bright light from the window falls on her.
the-courtyard-of-a-house-in-delft
A woman and a child stand in a corridor next to a sunny courtyard, with a bucket and a broom. Pieter de Hooch painted it in 1658, and the light and the brick make it very peaceful.
the-flight-into-egypt
Mary, Joseph and the baby Jesus travel through a rocky landscape, with a donkey and a bright sky. Nicolas Poussin painted it in 1658.
the-little-street

The front of two brick houses and a narrow alley, with a woman sewing at a doorway, and children playing on the ground. Johannes Vermeer painted it in about 1658, and it is one of his only pictures of the outside of a house.
the-young-mother
A young mother with a baby on her lap sits by a window, and a servant leans in from behind. Gerrit Dou painted it in 1658, with tiny, precise brushstrokes.
infanta-margarita-teresa-in-a-blue-dress

A young girl in a wide blue dress with silver trim stands with her hand on a table and her fair hair in ribbons. Diego Velázquez painted the Infanta Margarita in 1659 to send to her relatives in Vienna.
moses-smashing-the-tablets-of-the-law
Moses holds up the stone tablets of the Ten Commandments over his head and is about to throw them down because of the people's sin. Rembrandt painted it in 1659.
a-wooded-marsh
A swampy forest with dead trees and murky water, under a heavy sky with a distant light. Jacob van Ruisdael painted it in about 1660, and the quiet moodiness of the scene is full of feeling.
immaculate-conception-of-el-escorial
Mary, in a white dress and a blue cloak, floats on a crescent moon among angels, with her hands crossed on her chest. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1660.
rebecca-and-eliezer
A young woman at a well gives water to a servant and his camels, and her friends watch. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1660, from a Bible story.
the-birth-of-the-virgin
Women prepare the newborn Mary for her bath, while angels float above in a golden light. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1660, in a warm, family scene.
the-immaculate-conception-of-los-venerables
Mary floats up on a cloud with a crescent moon at her feet, surrounded by cherubs and clouds. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1660, and it is one of his many versions of this subject.
the-interview-of-luis-xiv-and-felipe-iv-in-the-island-o

Two kings meet on a floating pavilion in a river on the border of France and Spain, with many courtiers on both banks. Jacques Laumosnier painted it in about 1660, and it was part of the peace between the two countries.
the-letter-by-gerard-ter-borch
A woman in a white satin dress sits at a table, writing a letter, and a girl in the back watches her. Gerard ter Borch painted it in about 1660, and the satin skirt is the star.
the-milkmaid

A woman in a yellow bodice and blue apron pours milk very steadily from a jug into a bowl, in a plain room with light from the window. Johannes Vermeer painted it in about 1660, and every little thing, even the bread crumbs, shines.
the-sick-child
A mother holds a pale, sick child on her lap and looks at her sadly, in a quiet room. Gabriel Metsu painted it in about 1660, and it is a tender picture of care.
woman-with-a-water-jug

A young woman in a blue gown and a white cap opens a window with one hand and holds a jug with the other, in a quiet, light room. Johannes Vermeer painted it in about 1662, and the soft light on the cloth is beautiful.
a-woman-preparing-bread-and-butter-for-a-boy
A woman spreads butter on a slice of bread for a child in a bright room, where a dog sits and a sunlit courtyard shows through the doorway. Pieter de Hooch painted it in about 1661.
mother-lacing-her-bodice-beside-a-cradle
A mother laces her bodice by a cradle with a sleeping baby, and a young girl comes in from the corridor. Pieter de Hooch painted it in about 1661, and the picture is full of daylight.
the-doctor-s-visit-in-a-rich-interior

A doctor takes the pulse of a young woman, who is sick with a case of love, while her family looks anxiously on. Jan Steen painted it in about 1661, and the doctor's visit was a joke he liked to paint.
view-of-delft

The Dutch city of Delft sits across a canal under a gray sky, with a shaft of sunlight on the roofs, and a few people stand on the shore. Johannes Vermeer painted it in about 1660, and the French writer Marcel Proust called it the most beautiful painting in the world.
syndics-of-the-drapers-guild

Five cloth inspectors in black hats sit at a table in a red cloth, while a sixth stands behind, all looking up at us as if we had just come in. Rembrandt painted it in 1662, and it is one of the most famous group portraits.
the-music-lesson

A young woman stands at a harpsichord with her back to us, while a man stands near her, and a mirror shows her face. Johannes Vermeer painted it in about 1662, and the Latin words on the instrument mean 'Music is the companion of joy and balm for sorrow.'
beware-of-luxury-in-weelde-siet-toe

A messy room full of food, bad habits and silly behavior, with a mother who is asleep, a pig eating a rose and children playing with a dog. Jan Steen painted it in 1663, and the Dutch title means 'Beware of luxury'. A messy house is still called a Jan Steen household.
the-concert

Three musicians, a woman at the keyboard, another woman singing and a man with a lute, are in a room with a checked floor. Johannes Vermeer painted it in about 1663. It was stolen from a Boston museum in 1990 and has not been found.
regentesses-of-the-old-men-s-alms-house

Five elderly women in black dresses and white collars look out at us with serious faces, around a table. Frans Hals painted it in 1664, when he was about 84, and the hands and faces are painted with quick, wise brushstrokes.
the-astronomer

A man in a blue robe sits at a table and reaches for a globe, with an astrolabe and a book in front of him. Johannes Vermeer painted it in 1668, and the light from the window falls on his thoughtful face.
the-council-chamber-in-amsterdam-town-hall
A huge, bare, marble hall stands in the new Amsterdam Town Hall, with tiny people walking in it, and a doorway leads to another room. Pieter de Hooch painted it in about 1664.
the-good-shepherd
A young boy with long hair holds a lamb and a staff, looking out of a green landscape. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1664, and the Good Shepherd is Christ as a child.
woman-in-blue-reading-a-letter
A woman in a blue jacket stands, absorbed, reading a letter in front of a big map. Johannes Vermeer painted it in about 1664, and her calm face makes you wonder what the letter says.
as-the-old-sing-so-pipe-the-young

A family at a party sing and drink and smoke, and the grandparents do it too, while a small boy puffs on a pipe. Jan Steen painted it in about 1668, and the title is a proverb that children copy what the adults do.
girl-with-a-pearl-earring

A girl in a blue and yellow turban looks over her shoulder at us, with her lips slightly parted and a large pearl at her ear, against a dark background. Johannes Vermeer painted it in about 1665, and no one knows who she was. It is often called the Mona Lisa of the North.
infanta-margarita-teresa-in-a-pink-dress

A young girl in a wide pink dress with a silver trim stands with her hand on a table, with a feather in her hair. Juan Bautista Martínez del Mazo painted the Infanta in about 1665, working in the style of Velázquez, his father-in-law.
man-writing-a-letter
A man in a red coat stops writing a letter at a desk, a woman reads one nearby, in a matching painting. Gabriel Metsu painted it in about 1665, and the two paintings are hung side by side.
rest-on-the-flight-into-egypt
Joseph holds a donkey while Mary rests with the baby Jesus in her lap, and angels play music in the trees. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1665.
the-feast-of-saint-nicholas

Children in a family find gifts, and one little girl clutches a doll, while a boy who has been bad cries over a shoe filled with a switch. Jan Steen painted it in about 1665, and the festival of Saint Nicholas is the Dutch ancestor of Santa Claus.
the-flower-girl
A girl with a basket of flowers looks out with a half-smile and a flower in her hand. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1665, and she is wearing a white blouse with her shoulder bare.
woman-holding-a-balance

A woman holds an empty pair of scales in a sunlit room, with a mirror, a blue cloth and jewelry, while behind her a painting of the Last Judgment hangs on the wall. Johannes Vermeer painted it in about 1665.
woman-reading-a-letter
A woman in a yellow coat reads a letter beside a window while her maid peers in, with a curtain. Gabriel Metsu painted it in about 1665, and it is the second of a pair.
a-woman-feeding-a-parrot-with-a-page
A woman in a silk dress feeds a parrot in a cage, while a young servant boy holds a dish, in a rich room. Caspar Netscher painted it in 1666, and the satin glows.
the-art-of-painting

A painter in a funny puffy hat sits with his back to us, painting a woman in a blue dress with a laurel wreath and a trumpet, in a rich room with a huge map and a chandelier. Johannes Vermeer painted it in about 1666, and it is thought to be a picture of his own studio.
the-jewish-bride

A man in a red coat and a woman in gold hold hands, and he puts his hand gently on her chest. Rembrandt painted it in about 1667, and the thick, glowing paint is one of his late masterpieces, and the couple's identity is unknown.
el-retorno-del-hijo-gey

An old father with his hands on the shoulders of a ragged son kneeling before him, who has come home after wasting his money. Rembrandt painted it in about 1668, and it is one of his last and most moving paintings.
madonna-of-the-napkin
Mary holds the baby Jesus in her lap, with a soft smile, in a gentle glow. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1668, and the legend says he painted it on a napkin for a cook.
saint-francis-embracing-christ-on-the-cross
A monk in a brown robe hugs Christ, who leans down from the cross and puts an arm around him. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1668.
the-geographer

A man in a blue gown leans over a table covered with maps, holding a pair of compasses, and looks up toward the window. Johannes Vermeer painted it in about 1668, and a globe sits on the cupboard behind him.
the-happy-family

A family sings and plays music together at a table with food and drink, while a little boy smokes a pipe and a baby holds a glass. Jan Steen painted it in about 1668, and the proverb says that as the old sing, so the young pipe.
wine-is-a-mocker

A drunk husband and a wife get rowdy in a messy room, while a boy plays with a cat and a servant tells everyone it's time to go home. Jan Steen painted it in about 1668, and the title means that wine makes a fool of you.
girl-with-a-flute

A young woman in a red hat and a blue and yellow coat holds a flute, in a close-up portrait. This was painted in the studio of Johannes Vermeer, in about 1669, and it is not thought to be by Vermeer himself.
the-lacemaker

A young woman bends her head over her tiny lace work, with threads falling from a sewing cushion, in a small canvas. Johannes Vermeer painted it in about 1669, and the red and white threads are blurred in the front while the work is sharp.
the-windmill-at-wijk-bij-duurstede

A huge windmill stands on a dike by a river, under a sky of great clouds, with a little boat on the water. Jacob van Ruisdael painted it in about 1670, and it is one of the most famous pictures of the Netherlands.
conversion-of-saint-paul
Saul falls from his horse and is blinded by a bright light from the sky, while his companions rush in. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1675.
man-reading-letter-to-a-woman
A man reads a letter aloud to a woman who sits quietly and listens, in a tidy room. Pieter de Hooch painted it in about 1675.
the-aranjuez-immaculate-conception
Mary, in white and blue, stands on a crescent moon among cherubs, with her hands crossed and her eyes up. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1675.
the-concert-borch
A woman at a table sings from a piece of music while a man accompanies her, in a room with a long, quiet shadow. Gerard ter Borch painted it in about 1675.
the-crucifixion-murillo
Christ hangs on the cross against a dark sky, with a soft light that shines on his body. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1675.
the-martyrdom-of-st-andrew
Saint Andrew is tied to an X-shaped cross, and looks up as light breaks through the clouds. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted it in about 1675.
samson-mocked-by-the-philistines
Samson, blinded and chained, is mocked by a crowd of people at a party, and he stands bowed and helpless. Jan Steen painted it in about 1676.
charles-ii-presented-with-a-pineapple

A king in a wig accepts a pineapple from his gardener, in a formal garden, in front of a big house. This painting from the 1670s is said to show the first pineapple grown in England, and it was a big treat for the king.
